title: Large Language Models for Anomaly Detection in Computational Workflows: From Supervised Fine-Tuning to In-Context Learning
problem: Anomaly detection in computational workflows relies on rule-based methods that struggle to identify novel anomalies and complex data patterns in workflow executions. Traditional approaches lack the ability to learn complex behavioral patterns from data.
motivation: Anomaly detection in computational workflows is critical for ensuring system reliability and security in complex distributed executions.
method: Two approaches are investigated: (1) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) where pretrained LLMs are fine-tuned on labeled data for sentence classification to identify anomalies, and (2) in-context learning (ICL) using prompts with task descriptions and examples to guide LLMs in few-shot anomaly detection without fine-tuning. The work evaluates zero-shot, few-shot ICL variants and chain-of-thought prompting for interpretability across multiple workflow datasets.
key_novelty: Applying large language models with both fine-tuned and prompt-based in-context learning approaches to workflow anomaly detection, enabling few-shot detection without expensive model retraining.
contributions: Application of LLMs for computational workflow anomaly detection with two distinct training paradigms
Comparative evaluation of supervised fine-tuning versus in-context learning effectiveness
Demonstration of generalization across multiple workflow datasets
Integration of chain-of-thought prompting for interpretability enhancement
primary_theme: LLM-based anomaly detection for computational workflows
